subject: science
title: Metals and Non-metals
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns, true/false or a short passage).

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (1) Al₂O₃ and CO₂ both show acidic as well as basic properties. (2) Metals are electropositive and non-metals are electronegative.
questions.answer: (1) False — Al₂O₃ is amphoteric but CO₂ is acidic only. (2) True

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (1) Roasting is heating sulphide ores strongly in the presence of oxygen. (2) Calcination converts carbonate ores into oxides.
Fill in the blanks: The chemical formula of rust is ________, and stainless steel is an alloy of iron with ________ and nickel.
Match: (1) Cinnabar (2) Thermite process — (a) ore of zinc (b) ore of mercury (c) welding of railway tracks (d) extraction of sodium
Fill in the blanks: A mineral from which a metal can be extracted profitably is called an ________; the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature is ________.
Write True (T) or False (F): (1) Silver displaces copper from copper sulphate solution. (2) Sodium can be cut with a knife.
questions.answer: (1) False — silver is less reactive than copper. (2) True

sections.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: The reddish-brown substance is —
The nail in tube B did not rust because —
Anhydrous calcium chloride in tube C —
Galvanisation means coating iron with —
The experiment shows that rusting needs —

sections.passage: Neha placed three clean iron nails in test tubes. Tube A had some tap water so that the nail was partly in water and partly in air. Tube B had boiled water covered by a layer of oil. Tube C was dry and contained anhydrous calcium chloride. After a week, only the nail in tube A was covered with a flaky reddish-brown substance. Her teacher said that the iron gate at home is painted, and buckets are made of galvanised iron, for the same reason.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: State two properties of gold that make it suitable for making ornaments.
questions.answer: Gold is very malleable and ductile, so it can be shaped into fine designs, and it is lustrous and does not corrode or tarnish (unreactive).

questions.q: What is galvanisation? Give one use.
questions.answer: Galvanisation is coating iron or steel with a thin layer of zinc to prevent rusting. Galvanised iron sheets are used for roofs, buckets, drums and trunks.

questions.q: What is rust? Write two conditions necessary for rusting.
questions.answer: Rust is hydrated ferric oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O), the reddish-brown flaky coating formed on iron. Rusting needs (1) oxygen (air) and (2) moisture (water).

or.q: Write balanced equations: (a) sodium burns in oxygen to give sodium oxide; (b) iron reacts with steam.

questions.q: Write two ways to prevent rusting.
questions.answer: Any two: painting; oiling or greasing; galvanisation (zinc coating); alloying (stainless steel).

or.q: Name (a) a metal soft enough to cut with a knife and the hardest non-metal; (b) a metal and a non-metal that are liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: What is the reactivity series? Arrange Cu, Fe, Na, Mg, Ag and Pb in decreasing order of reactivity.
questions.answer: The arrangement of metals in decreasing order of their reactivity is the reactivity (activity) series. Na > Mg > Fe > Pb > Cu > Ag.

questions.q: A copper wire is dipped in silver nitrate solution. What will you observe? Write the reaction.
questions.answer: A shiny grey-white deposit of silver forms on the wire and the solution turns blue, because copper is more reactive than silver. Cu + 2AgNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag.

or.q: Write the names and formulae of the oxides of nitrogen.
or.answer: Nitrous oxide N₂O, nitric oxide NO, dinitrogen trioxide N₂O₃, nitrogen dioxide NO₂, dinitrogen tetroxide N₂O₄, dinitrogen pentoxide N₂O₅.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is the nature of non-metal oxides? Write the equation for the reaction of SO₃ with water.
questions.answer: Most non-metal oxides are acidic — they dissolve in water to form acids and react with bases to form salts and water (CO, N₂O and NO are neutral). SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄ (sulphuric acid).

or.q: Name the ore of mercury and write the equations for the extraction of mercury from it.
or.answer: Cinnabar (HgS). It is roasted: 2HgS + 3O₂ → 2HgO + 2SO₂; on further heating the oxide decomposes: 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂.

questions.q: What is the thermite process? Name the metal used, write the balanced equation and give one use.
questions.answer: In the thermite process aluminium powder reduces a metal oxide such as iron(III) oxide; the reaction gives so much heat that the iron formed is molten. Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → 2Fe + Al₂O₃. It is used to weld railway tracks and broken machine parts.

questions.q: Zinc ores A and B give CO₂ and SO₂ respectively when heated. Identify A and B and write the steps, with equations, to obtain zinc from them.
questions.answer: A is zinc carbonate (calamine, ZnCO₃) and B is zinc sulphide (zinc blende, ZnS). Calcination of A: ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂. Roasting of B: 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂. Reduction of the oxide with carbon: ZnO + C → Zn + CO.
questions.note: October 2022 also asked why metals are electropositive and non-metals electronegative — metals lose valence electrons to form positive ions; non-metals gain electrons to form negative ions.

questions.q: Write four chemical properties of metals with equations.
questions.answer: (1) With oxygen they form basic oxides: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. (2) With water they form hydroxides or oxides and hydrogen: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. (3) With dilute acids they give hydrogen: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. (4) A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its salt: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.

questions.q: A silver coin is put in copper sulphate solution and a copper coin in silver nitrate solution. What happens in each case and why?
questions.answer: Silver coin in CuSO₄: no reaction, because silver is less reactive than copper. Copper coin in AgNO₃: silver deposits on the coin and the solution turns blue, because copper is more reactive than silver and displaces it: Cu + 2AgNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Distinguish between metals and non-metals on the basis of five physical properties. Name a metal and a non-metal that are exceptions to any two of these.
questions.answer: Metals are malleable and ductile, non-metals brittle; metals have lustre, non-metals generally do not; metals are sonorous, non-metals not; metals are good conductors of heat and electricity, non-metals poor; metals are usually hard with high density, non-metals soft with low density. Exceptions: mercury is a liquid metal; sodium is a soft metal; graphite is a non-metal that conducts electricity; iodine and graphite are lustrous; diamond is a very hard non-metal.

questions.q: What is corrosion? Describe an activity to show that both air and moisture are needed for rusting. Describe four methods of preventing rusting.
questions.answer: Corrosion is the slow destruction of a metal by the action of air and moisture; the rusting of iron forms Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. Activity: nail A in a test tube with some water (air and water), nail B in boiled water covered with oil (no air), nail C with anhydrous calcium chloride (no moisture); after a few days only nail A rusts. Prevention: (1) painting; (2) oiling and greasing; (3) galvanisation — coating with zinc; (4) alloying — stainless steel (iron with chromium and nickel).

questions.q: How are metals of low, medium and high reactivity extracted from their ores? Give one example with equations for each.
questions.answer: Low reactivity — heating alone: cinnabar 2HgS + 3O₂ → 2HgO + 2SO₂; 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂. Medium reactivity — the sulphide or carbonate ore is roasted or calcined to the oxide and reduced with carbon: 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂; ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂; ZnO + C → Zn + CO (or by aluminium in the thermite process). High reactivity — electrolysis of the molten compound: molten NaCl gives sodium at the cathode (Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na) and chlorine at the anode (2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻).
